executive_summary:
In the window from 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-01, ARI3 collected 4,051 raw source records from 80 outlet domains. Final signal evidence was deduplicated so exact mirrors and syndicated or translated versions of the same publication count as one report evidence unit. The editor retained 19 signals. The largest by item count are sneaker (66 items from 15 outlets), denim (26 from 17), minimalism (14 from 9), suede (14 from 10) and vintage (14 from 11). Sneaker is concentrated, with 32 of its items from two outlets, mostly release coverage, and sneaker heels recur as a sub-theme. Denim is the most widely spread, across 17 outlets. Minimalism appears often in headlines that set it against another style.

Autumn footwear and outerwear recur in loafer, trench, leather jacket, burgundy, ballet flat and bomber. Oversized (10 items from 5 outlets) is tied to brand campaigns, three of them for Balenciaga's skiwear. The smaller clusters are wide-leg, streetwear, fringe, leopard, maximalism and kitten heel, which meets the report minimum (2 items from 2 outlets). These are patterns in the sources ARI3 collects, which were 89.2% editorial in this window. They do not measure consumer adoption or what people wear.

top_signals.name: sneaker
top_signals.evidence: Release coverage dominates: Nike Air Force 1, Air Jordan and Air Max releases, the New Balance 990, 991v2 and trail sneakers, Travis Scott with Nike, Corteiz with Nike, Wales Bonner with adidas and the return of G-Unit Reebok sneakers. Sneaker heels recur, including Nike's Ovolo revival and a WWD piece on the hybrid. Styling pieces cover sneakers at work, with baggy jeans and in low-profile shapes, Salomon in Paris and black sneakers, with Italian-language GQ Italia and Vogue Italia and German-language Vogue Germany headlines (translated). Two headlines present other shoes as the alternative to sneakers.
top_signals.index_note: The signal has 66 items from 15 outlets, editorial 61 and retail 5, on every day of the window. highsnobiety.com contributes 18 items and wwd.com 14, so 32 of the 66 come from two outlets. The editor labeled it recurring.
top_signals.human_editor_note: Editorial view: sneakers will always be that girl. So much fashion room. So much style.

limitations: Items are counted as style only when the ARI3 style classifier (frozen v0.0.2) gives a confident yes. On a 150-item prospective holdout of articles published after the classifier was frozen, its accuracy was 0.833, below its pre-registered 0.85 criterion (EXP-003A, H2 not supported). The editor reviews every evidence item used in this report.
In this window, 1,732 of 4,051 items (42.8%) received a not-sure prediction set and were excluded from style-positive counts.

In this window, 89.2% of collected items came from the editorial sector and 94.7% from the editorial group (editorial, trade intelligence and independent criticism). The stored corpus as a whole is 89.1% editorial sector.

The window has 0 items from social platforms, which are not collected, and 2 from resale sources. The report describes the language of the collected sources, not style culture, fashion consumers or the public at large.
Signal interpretation and evidence review are done by one editor.
ARI3 stores each item's headline and feed excerpt, not the full article.
0 of the window's 4051 items were stored before 2026-09-30, so their first-seen times are reconstructed from earlier records, not recorded as they happened.
Seven ambiguous lexicon terms (western, brat, demure, lace, bow, sustainable, glamour) are left out of every count until their uses are checked one by one.

Exact mirrors and syndicated, translated or lightly re-edited versions of the same publication across publisher domains are collapsed to one report evidence unit. The frozen source snapshot retains the raw records.
ai_assistance: ARI3’s deterministic pipeline surfaced candidate signals and bound the report to a frozen evidence snapshot. An AI assistant drafted the executive summary, evidence text, and index notes using only the locked report evidence, including translations of non-English headlines. The editor selected and merged signals, set labels and confidence overrides, pruned evidence, reviewed the drafted text, wrote the editor notes, and approved the final report.
